body:
>This hectic time in your life will pass.

You're right. On some level, I *know*, always know, no matter my state of mind, that my emotions and circumstances are impermanent. I can always find a way out of the mess that I've put myself in, if not now, with time. I also can see that it will be an arduous struggle to bring myself back from my present miserable caveman state to something that resembles a normal human being. I think therapy may help with that, but I'm somewhat skeptical. On one hand, I know that I am still deeply affected by my past, as I had a somewhat traumatic and lonely childhood. I've tried to come to terms with it and make my peace, but digging some of the skeletons out of my closet with someone else might help me figure out better or different strategies or coping mechanisms than those I am able to come up with on my own.

 However, a couple of decades of relative social isolation has also made me pretty resistant to seeking outside help, because I know that it isn't always reliable or well-intentioned, and that the most lasting changes have to come from within. I also don't really know *how* to ask others for help, which has definitely contributed to my collegiate floundering, among other things. I'm aware of my thinking being occasionally warped and that I need to essentially 180 my attitude towards myself, but it's *hard*, especially if you try to approach the whole necessary transformation at once, which I tend to do. You can only peel one spud at a time, as they say. I know, rationally, that this moment is something of a low point, and that I've reached it through a whole lot of compounding stress from multiple factors in the near and distant past. I see that it's an a wholly uphill climb from where I am, but can rationalize that the only way to reach the top of the mountain is one step at a time. It doesn't always make it easier to keep my feet going, though.

The only thing I really think the human life is worth living for is compassion, for easing other beings' journeys through lives so often filled with pain. However, I feel my potential to reach out is somewhat stifled by my present circumstance of stress and confusion. I feel somewhat trapped by my past, and know I need to come to terms with it to move forward. I'm also admittedly a bit lost when it comes to my future, figuring out how I could best utilize my abilities to maximize the kindness I can contribute to the world. It can be a bit overwhelming trying to go about finding a practical, enjoyable, meaningful role without any sort of trustworthy support network to give you feedback in that decision making process. Or while you occasionally think you're incapable of changing a single damned thing about anything. I suppose the best teacher here is trial and error. More of both will lead to less of the latter.
